scores.evidence: every booking re-checks the slot against the live database at commit
scores.rationale: Technical claims (CDC semantics, fencing, HL7 SIU/ADT message types, DNS-TTL switching, write-pause rationale against split-brain) are accurate and precise, including the subtle consistency areas.

scores.evidence: At the one moment the database writer switches over, new bookings pause for up to 60 seconds.
scores.rationale: It solves the actual request, honestly resolves the 'zero downtime' ambiguity, covers all implied core needs, and is credibly buildable by a realistic hospital IT team.

scores.evidence: Exactly one database accepts bookings at any time, protected by a fencing mechanism.
scores.rationale: The single-writer decision, routing layer, CDC direction and phase dependencies are honored consistently everywhere, with cross-cutting identity, logging and consistency handled uniformly per phase.

scores.evidence: 14 consecutive days with: 100% checksum match, zero scheduling-rule violations, CDC lag p99 < 5 s
scores.rationale: Each phase has measurable exit checks tied to the specific risks (shadow-match rate, write replay, three rehearsals, rollback drill), riskiest assumptions tested in Phase 0, and validation continues post-cutover.

scores.evidence: Assumptions to confirm in week 1. These can change the plan
scores.rationale: Design-critical assumptions (vendor support, client type, DB engine, BAA, RTO/RPO) are explicit with revisit triggers per decision stating how the plan changes if wrong.

scores.evidence: Worst failure: Split-brain. Both the old and new databases accept bookings at the same moment
scores.rationale: The hardest domain failures (double-booking, PHI leakage, link outage, CDC lag/drift, failed interface messages) each get concrete detection, containment and recovery, including rollback triggers and reconciliation rule checks.

scores.evidence: Written runbook, with a timed step for each action and named owners.
scores.rationale: IaC deployment, versioned schema migrations, dashboards on domain-meaningful signals (CDC lag, SIU acks), on-call alerting, rehearsed rollback and named ownership make this operable by a realistic team.

scores.evidence: Cost optimisation (reserved capacity, right-sizing). Pull forward after 60 days of steady usage data.
scores.rationale: Costs are only a deferred bullet: dual-running infrastructure, redundant private links, DMS, licensing and engineering effort — the dominant cost drivers — are never estimated or controlled.

scores.evidence: Reverse CDC (cloud→on-prem) stays live for 30–90 days, with the on-prem database fenced read-only.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse moves get explicit exit paths (reverse CDC, same-engine replatform, permanent routing switch), while reversible choices get fast defaults with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: Keep the monolith as it is. A migration is not the time to re-architect. Change one variable at a time.
scores.rationale: Builds only the routing switch, reconciliation jobs and runbooks, explicitly defers rewrites, active-active and new features; every added element serves the no-downtime or compliance need.

scores.evidence: Phases (ordered by dependency; widest impact first within each)
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: concrete Phase-0 slice, dependency-justified ordering, specific decisions, checkable exit criteria per phase, and stated adaptations if assumptions or results disappoint.

checklist.evidence: BAA signed before any PHI moves. Private link only. PHI scrubbed from logs.
Every interface has been repointed to the cloud and back in a test environment.

At least 3 full rehearsals on a production-sized clone, including one rollback rehearsal.
